extracted.intended_audience: VA officials, VA health care practitioners, legal/regulatory stakeholders, and commenters on NPDB rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Final rule text and responses to public comment regarding VA's removal of 38 CFR part 46 and reliance on HHS NPDB regulations, MOU, and VA policy to govern National Practitioner Data Bank reporting and related procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory consolidation: follow HHS NPDB regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) adopts as final, without changes, a proposed rule to remove its regulations governing the National Practitioner Data Bank (NPDB). Instead, VA will rely on Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) regulations that govern the NPDB, a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) between VA and HHS, and VA policy and procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removing VA's separate NPDB regulations reduces the total number of NPDB authorities and simplifies the regulatory framework; VA will support the HHS regulatory framework through updated VA policies and an MOU with HHS.

rubrics_metrics.name: APA judicial-review standard for regulatory changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Administrative Procedures Act (APA), the Secretary's decision to create, amend, or remove regulations will only be reversed if a court finds it 'arbitrary, capricious, an abuse of discretion, or otherwise not in accordance with law' or meets other listed 5 U.S.C. 706 standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: VA need not provide a 'compelling reason' but must provide a rational basis connecting facts and the chosen action; cite 5 U.S.C. 706(1)-(2)(A)-(D).

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for MOU and VA policy to address HHS/VA conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: Because certain provisions of the HHS NPDB regulations conflict with VA's role and responsibility as a Federal agency, an MOU with HHS and VA internal policies and procedures are necessary to address and avoid such conflicts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: VA will use the MOU and policies to supplement HHS regulations and to set VA-specific procedures more quickly than through regulatory amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of reportable actions: include exclusions and adjudicated actions
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS NPDB regulations require reporting of exclusions from participation in Federal or State health care programs and other adjudicated actions or decisions as required in 45 CFR 60.15 and 60.16; VA's 38 CFR part 46 did not explicitly address these reporting requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removing VA regulations and following HHS rules will resolve inconsistencies and clarify whether such actions must be reported by VA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency of definitions with HHS regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions in VA's 38 CFR 46.1 are not wholly consistent with those found in 45 CFR 60.3, creating potential confusion about applicable requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopting HHS definitions via reliance on HHS regulations reduces definitional inconsistency; VA policies/MOU should align definitions where VA-specific treatment is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may be reported / voluntary reporting of other licensed practitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: VA regulations only permit reporting of adverse actions against physicians and dentists (38 CFR 46.12), while HHS additionally authorizes voluntary reporting of other licensed health care practitioners (45 CFR 60.12(a)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It was unclear under VA regulations whether VA could voluntarily report other licensed practitioners; following HHS regulations with VA policy/MOU clarifies voluntary reporting authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for reporting malpractice payments
rubrics_metrics.description: VA's practice (per VHA Directive 1100.17) is to report a malpractice payment to the NPDB only after a majority of the VA review panel determines the payment was 'related to substandard care, professional incompetence, or professional misconduct'; by contrast, commenter asserted HHS regulations require all payments be reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: VA clarifies that removing its regulations will not alter its processes for reviewing and reporting malpractice payments; VHA Directive 1100.17 remains in effect to preserve the existing threshold for reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review panel composition requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: VA's existing policy requires that when reviewing malpractice claims, at least one member of the medical malpractice review panel must be from the same profession and specialty as the practitioner under review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement will remain in effect via VHA Directive 1100.17 even after removing VA regulations, to preserve integrity and due process in review processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition/clarification on peer-to-peer reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: There is nothing in the HHS regulation that requires or permits a 'peer' to report a provider subjected to an adverse privileging action; voluntary reporting authority rests with health care entities, not individual peers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: VA will maintain its existing prohibition on peer-to-peer reporting through policy and MOU as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility and speed of updating via policy/MOU vs regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: The process to update VA's policies and the MOU is much quicker than the process for updating VA's regulations, which requires notice-and-comment rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relying on policy and MOU allows VA to implement VA-specific procedures more efficiently, reducing potential for confusion or conflict between different sets of regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with other Federal agencies' NPDB approach
rubrics_metrics.description: No other Federal agency maintains its own set of NPDB regulations; other agencies use HHS statutory/regulatory authority, MOUs, and internal policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopting the same approach as other agencies reduces inconsistencies across Federal NPDB compliance practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collective bargaining obligations for hybrid title 38 employees
rubrics_metrics.description: If any changes to VA's NPDB reporting policy in the future would impact the terms and conditions of hybrid title 38 bargaining unit employees, such proposed changes would be subject to applicable collective bargaining rules and regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: VA must provide notice to applicable unions and/or bargain over the impact and implementation of such changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complementary actions to address OIG recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Removal of the NPDB regulation is only part of a larger plan to meet the 2022 VA OIG recommendations: VA is updating VHA Directive 1100.17, updating the MOU with HHS, and enhancing oversight and training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy, MOU updates, oversight enhancements, and training will complement the regulatory change to improve compliance and reporting processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Orders: regulatory impact and review requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Executive Orders 12866, 13563, and 14192 direct agencies to assess costs and benefits of regulatory alternatives, quantify impacts, harmonize rules, and promote flexibility; the Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs determined this rulemaking is not a significant regulatory action under Executive Order 12866.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should assess net benefits, distributive impacts, equity, and whether actions are 'significant' under EO 12866 when rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Flexibility Act certification
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary certifies that this final rule will not have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities; the rule affects only individuals who are VA employees or independent contractors acting on behalf of VA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursuant to 5 U.S.C. 605(b), initial and final regulatory flexibility analysis requirements do not apply if the rule will not have significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfunded Mandates assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Unfunded Mandates Reform Act (2 U.S.C. 1532), agencies must prepare an assessment before issuing any rule that may result in expenditures of $100 million or more in any one year; this final rule will have no such effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether the $100 million threshold (adjusted for inflation) is met to trigger the Unfunded Mandates assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: This final rule contains no provisions constituting a collection of information under the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995 (44 U.S.C. 3501-3521).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify whether any regulatory provision creates an information collection requiring OMB approval under the PRA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Congressional Review Act submission and designation
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to the Congressional Review Act (5 U.S.C. 801 et seq.), the Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs designated this rule as not satisfying the criteria under 5 U.S.C. 804(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure timely submission to Congress and proper designation under the CRA requirements when finalizing a rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official publication and legal notice practices
rubrics_metrics.description: XML renditions on FederalRegister.gov are informational and unofficial; the PDF on govinfo.gov is the official electronic format and only official editions provide legal notice to the public and judicial notice to the courts under 44 U.S.C. 1503 & 1507.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the PDF on govinfo.gov for legal research and citation; do not rely solely on the XML prototype for legal notice.
